metadata.title: Basic Safety and Essential Performance of Medical Electrical Equipment, Medical Electrical Systems, and Laboratory Medical Equipment - Standards Specific Information for the Accreditation Scheme for Conformity Assessment (ASCA) Program: Draft Guidance for Industry, Accreditation Bodies, Testing Laboratories, and Food and Drug Administration Staff
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics

candidates.statement: If the testing laboratory has questions or concerns associated with the device manufacturer’s 396 proposed test plan (e.g., essential performance(s), unclear acceptance criteria), they should 397 discuss such concerns/questions with the device manufacturer, preferentially in advance of 398 finalization of the test plan. If those concerns or questions remain unresolved, the testing 399 laboratory should consider detailing the potential issues in the ASCA Summary Test Report 400 (e.g., in the Concerns Identified section in the example provided in Appendix B of this 401 guidance). 402 (1) Essential Performance 403 FDA recommends the device manufacturer specifies the essential performance(s) of their 404 device. Additionally, testing laboratories should have expertise in the terminology, 405 evaluation, and performance of the FDA-recognized consensus standards to assist a device 406 manufacturer in understanding the concept of essential performance and how it might relate 407 to their device, as appropriate. 408
candidates.context: A. Test plan development as a collaboration between 387 device manufacturers and testing laboratories 388 As described in the draft ASCA Program guidance document, FDA recommends device 389 manufacturers consult with ASCA-accredited testing laboratories when developing a 390 comprehensive test plan for their device. FDA encourages a collaborative relationship 391 between the device manufacturer and testing laboratory wherever possible. Such 392 collaboration may help to ensure the appropriate selection and use of FDA-recognized 393 consensus standards and test methods. 394 We recommend that testing laboratories and device manufacturers consider the content of the 410 AAMI consensus report CR500:2019, Basic Introduction to the IEC 60601 Series, which 411 includes clarifications to help device manufacturers understand “essential performance.” 5
